posts.title: Issue 11: Pump prices double in the delta as the military seeks a record defence budget
posts.dek: 6–12 Nov 2026. Petrol doubles in Ayeyarwady, a K10 trillion defence request, and two street-rate trackers that no longer agree.
posts.body_md: First published on the [Burma/Myanmar Economics Monitor Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61588989971929).

sections.label: Petrol per litre in nine Ayeyarwady townships, from K5,500–7,500 in October
sections.text_md:
- **Why:** a station owner says the energy ministry cut monthly fuel quotas, pushing drivers onto the black market.
- **Sittwe:** rice over K200,000 a sack, cooking oil K18,000–25,500 a litre, onions up to K15,000 a viss (DMG, 12 Nov).
- **Yangon list rate**, unchanged all week: Octane 92 K4,530, diesel K4,555 a litre (Irrawaddy list, 10–12 Nov).

sections.label: Army letter now needed to move rice, fuel, oil and medicine on the Taungoo–Leiktho road
sections.text_md:
- Loads without the LIB 603 commander's letter are confiscated; a bag of rice in Leiktho has nearly doubled.
- Thailand reopened the unofficial Myawaddy–Mae Sot crossings on 6 Nov after a seven-day closure (DVB, 10 Nov).
- TNLA has barred large trucks on the Namkham–Mong Wee road until 31 Jan (Frontier, 10 Nov; armed-group claim).

sections.label: Share of hot-season power demand that generation will meet; cuts continue through 2027
sections.source: Deputy energy minister via Frontier, 13 Nov
sections.text_md:
- Demand forecast 5,010 MW against 3,540 MW of generation.
- Unilever is reported to be handing its Myanmar companies to local owners (Khit Thit via BCRN, 7 Nov; single source, unconfirmed).
- Karenni IEC offers interest-free microloans to 50 small businesses (DVB, 6 Nov).

sections.label: Street rate per US$ on 12 Nov — two trackers, same day
sections.text_md:
- The two series disagree in level and direction after 9 Nov, so treat the level as uncertain.
- Defence request for 2026–27 is over K10 trillion, against K7.95 trillion first allocated this year (Than Lwin Times via BNI, 12 Nov).
- Cash withdrawals capped at K10M a week per person; exporters may now hold FX 45 days, up from 30 (BBC Burmese; Eleven, 10 Nov).

sections.label: ≈US$3,000 taken per Chinese national at three checkpoints out of Shwe Kokko
sections.text_md:
- Troops reportedly charge 10,000–100,000 baht a vehicle for scam-centre traffic at nine Mon/Karen checkpoints (KIC via BNI, 12 Nov).
- Arakan fertiliser now K280,000–400,000 a sack, from under K100,000 (DMG, 12 Nov).
- Myothit villages pay a K20,000 monthly "conscription fee" per household (Myaelatt Athan, 11 Nov; single source).

posts.title: Issue 10: The kyat slides past K4,900 as blockades lift dry-zone prices several-fold
posts.dek: 28 Oct – 5 Nov 2026. The military tightens its grip on foreign exchange; Myingyan and Manaung run short of food.
posts.body_md: First published on the [Burma/Myanmar Economics Monitor Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61588989971929).

sections.label: Onions per viss in blockaded Myingyan District, from K1,000–1,500
sections.source: Mandalay Free Press / Taungtha News, 26–27 Oct (single source)
sections.text_md:
- Coarse rice ~K250,000 a sack (was ~K100,000+); eggs K600+ each.
- **Why:** since early September villagers have been barred from buying in town, with heavy gate fees on the Myingyan–Myothit road.
- Manaung Island (Rakhine): rice over K120,000 a basket (Narinjara via BNI, 30 Oct).

sections.label: Thailand's closure of unofficial Myawaddy–Mae Sot crossings, from 30 Oct
sections.text_md:
- The AA/ULA signed an MOU for a Paletwa–Mizoram trade point on 29 Oct, suspended since 14 Sep (DVB; DMG).
- Buses on the Yangon–Mandalay Expressway can no longer carry cargo, closing a cheap route for farmers (DVB, 3 Nov).

sections.label: Japan–Myanmar trade in FY2025-26, as Japan lobbies FATF to delist Myanmar
sections.text_md:
- The US Integrated Country Strategy targets at least three deals of ~US$5M and links peace talks to rare earths (Reuters via DVB, 4 Nov).
- MNDAA reportedly offers land and residency to Chinese investors putting in ¥500,000+ (single source).

sections.label: Street rate per US$ on 5 Nov, up 4.8% from K4,685 on 28 Oct
sections.text_md:
- The central bank says it sold US$2.22B of FX from April to 5 Nov, US$1.70B for fuel, edible oil and fertiliser, and threatened unlicensed dealers (CBM via Eleven, 6 Nov).
- FATF kept Myanmar on its blacklist on 30 Oct; review in Feb 2027 (Frontier, 2 Nov).

sections.label: Conscription levy per household in Kyonpyaw, up from K20,000
sections.source: Khit Thit via Frontier, 2 Nov (single source)
sections.text_md:
- Villages pay K10M if they send no conscripts.
- Gate fees on the Myingyan–Myothit road; drone strikes on Karenni farmers during harvest (DVB, 29 Oct).

posts.title: Issue 9: A weak kyat and import curbs push up household costs as fighting chokes Rakhine and Muse trade
posts.dek: 15–27 Oct 2026. Cooking gas up 50% in a week, palm-oil permits cut, and the kyat past K4,700.
posts.body_md: First published on the [Burma/Myanmar Economics Monitor Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61588989971929).

sections.label: Yangon cooking gas (LPG), K12,000 → K18,000 a viss in one week
sections.text_md:
- **Why:** about 90% of LPG is imported and paying for it needs scarce dollars.
- Octane 92 is K4,965/L in Mon State; importers there buy dollars at the street rate (BNI/IMNA, 23 Oct).

sections.label: Palm-oil import permits cut, so Yangon cooking oil keeps rising
sections.text_md:
- The Rakhine–India route is effectively closed: Kyauktaw's market stopped trading and Paletwa's cargo jetty was hit on 18–19 Oct.
- Mandalay–Muse road restricted: the Hsipaw bridge is still closed (Frontier, 15 Oct).

sections.label: Small Magway oil wells and refineries destroyed, wiping out village incomes
sections.text_md:
- Yangon luxury-condo projects have stalled (Myanmar Now, 21 Oct).
- Fishing workers in southern Rakhine are about 80% jobless (BNI, 22 Oct).

sections.label: Street rate per US$ on 27 Oct, against the official K2,100
sections.text_md:
- Parliament approved K2.1 trillion in central-bank borrowing on 14 Oct.
- Remittances: US$5.6B in 2025 is the only sourced figure (Myanmar Now, 19 Oct). The "$7–8B a year" claim has no source.

sections.label: Drop in Kyauktaw market sales since the 28 Sep airstrike
sections.text_md:
- Only 662 of 14,730 detained after the KK Park raid were prosecuted (DVB, 22 Oct).
- The SSPP collects conscription money twice a month, K40,000–100,000 each time (Frontier, 23 Oct).

posts.title: Issue 8: Onion and egg prices jump in Rakhine and Mon as gold trades far above the reference price
posts.body_md: First published on the [Burma/Myanmar Economics Monitor Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61588989971929).

sections.label: Onions per viss in Rakhine, up from K10,000
sections.text_md:
- Mon onions K10,000 a viss, from K7,000 in mid-September (IMNA, 5 Oct).
- Rakhine eggs K700 each, from K500 (DVB, 14 Oct).

sections.label: Price of a Jinko solar panel, up from K550,000 in August
sections.text_md: - Solar batteries rose from K7.2M to K9.2M as households and shops buy their way around blackouts.

sections.label: Market price of a tical of 24K gold, against the YGEA reference of K7.1M
sections.text_md: - Remittances: 25% must go through official banks, plus a 2% income tax; workers must show proof to leave (Labour Ministry, 4 Oct).

sections.label: Scam takings by the Wei clan, sentenced in China
sections.text_md: - Three death sentences, three life terms and 55 jailed.
